commits.edited_message:
pcre2grep: track the file position as int64_t, not int (#1020)

When regexec is not given REG_STARTEND, the subject is a C string. Reject
a start offset past that string before reporting a match.

Co-authored-by: Manohar Paturi <manoharpaturi@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

pcre2posix: do not truncate the subject length to int in regexec (#1022)

Once the REG_STARTEND span has been copied into size_t offsets, the flag
is spent: it does not change how the pattern is matched.

Co-authored-by: Manohar Paturi <manoharpaturi@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

posix: validate REG_STARTEND offsets and NULL pointer arguments (#1009)

After the offsets are taken, an interior start into a C string must lie
within the subject. REG_STARTEND is not a match option and is cleared
once the span has been read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
regexec's REG_STARTEND path is required to honour an explicit so/eo span and must not call strlen on that subject (the span need not be NUL-terminated). The overflow appears only when two of the three edits are combined, so reverting any one of them leaves a strlen of the caller's buffer reachable.
5b71939 adds a post-match check that strlen's the subject only when REG_STARTEND is clear, and rejects a start past that C string. On its own the flag is still set for a STARTEND call, so the new read is skipped; ordinary regexec subjects are NUL-terminated, so the extra strlen is in-bounds and the match result is unchanged.
abbf691, while widening so/eo to PCRE2_SIZE, clears REG_STARTEND after the offsets have been copied. Nothing added in that commit reads the flag again, and pcre2_match is still called with length eo-so, so a STARTEND match is unchanged and no strlen is introduced.
2d3a98a, while validating arguments, strlen's only when the flag is already clear and so>0, then clears REG_STARTEND itself. Without abbf691's earlier clear, a STARTEND call still has the flag set at this check, so this commit does not measure the subject; it only drops the flag. Without 5b71939, nothing after that drop measures it either.
Any pair is enough: abbf691's clear makes 2d3a98a's so>0 check call strlen; abbf691's clear makes 5b71939's post-match check call strlen; 2d3a98a's own clear makes 5b71939's check call strlen even if abbf691 did not drop the flag. The credited probe uses REG_STARTEND with rm_so>0 on an 8-byte buffer that has no trailing NUL, which is in-contract for REG_STARTEND, so every pair overflows and no single edit does. Fixing only one commit's diff leaves one of the other pairs intact.
